transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20260823-83b7c2a1
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Product), Maya (CSM); Samir (CTO), Lena (Platform Eng), Tom (SRE), Renee (Security)

Auto-summary: Quick demo of Redwood's traffic governor (org/project key model), live Console walkthrough of quota slices, and discussion of dedicated vs hosted routing policies. Customer asks about burst fencing, per-team billing, and audit logs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. uh quick intro from our side, I'm Alex, AE on the account, Priya will run through the demo, Jordan's here for product questions.
[00:12] Samir (CTO): Thanks Alex, quickly, our main thing is we have two workloads: real-time inference for search (p99 latency goals) and nightly batch embeddings. Need a pattern to keep the real-time path stable during big batch spikes.
[00:26] Priya (SE): Totally. We'll cover org/project key topologies, quota slices, and then the fairburst/backpressure policies — how Redwood routes by policy so you can keep your low-latency lanes isolated.
[00:38] Lena (Platform Eng): Quick Q, when you say project key, is that like API keys per team or per environment? We already tag keys in our infra, curious about enforcement granularity.
[00:52] Priya (SE): Good question. You can do either — org keys map to billing/parent quotas, projects are finer grained for teams or apps. In the Console you'll see how keys map to namespace, and you can attach quota slices and routing priority.
[01:08] Tom (SRE): And if a batch job tries to burst, does Redwood throttle aggressively or queue? We need to avoid long tail latencies.
[01:20] Priya (SE): We have a few levers: per-key concurrency limits, token-based rate quotas, and a fairburst allocator that reserves steady-state capacity then allows controlled bursts with backpressure if thresholds reached. You can set graceful fallback to a cheaper model variant or a different region.
[01:40] Renee (Security): For compliance, we need audit logs for key creation and token usage, also KMS integration for key material. Is that supported on private deployments?
[01:52] Jordan (Product): Yes, Private and Dedicated both support customer KMS/HSM and detailed audit trails. Hosted has a SOC2 report and retention tiers; we'll share the docs.
[02:06] Alex (AE): I'll drop the SOC2 and a sample network diagram after the call.
[02:12] Samir (CTO): Great. Priya, can you show the Console?
[02:18] Priya (SE): Sure live now — pulling up the Console. bear with me, screen share lag.
[02:32] [screen share noise]
[02:45] Priya (SE): This is the Traffic Governor view. On the left you can see Organizations, then Projects. I've set up an org-level cap, and two project slices — search-service-project (high priority) and embeddings-batch (low priority).
[03:04] Priya (SE): Notice the allocation slider — you can allocate a percent of org throughput to a project. We also have burst quota allowances — here I allowed embeddings-batch a short burst runway of 3x for scheduled windows.
[03:22] Lena (Platform Eng): So that burst is time-bound — we can white-list a cron job?
[03:28] Priya (SE): Exactly, you can create windowed policies, e.g., nightly 02:00-05:00 UTC, and bind them to service accounts or project keys.
[03:38] Tom (SRE): How do you handle KV cache collisions or shared prefix caching across projects? If two projects access the same model, do caches get evicted?
[03:50] Priya (SE): The runtime maintains per-project KV caches by default to avoid noisy neighbor eviction. You can enable a shared cache for read-heavy models, but that's a deliberate config to trade cost for hit-rate.
[04:06] Samir (CTO): Benchmarks — any public numbers for p50/p95 when using dedicated pools vs hosted?
[04:16] Jordan (Product): We have model-specific performance profiles; for example on a c4-style instance (GPU family X) p95 for a 512-token llama-like model is ~90ms in Dedicated with optimized kernels, hosted is similar but depends on multi-tenant load; we'll send a model profile sheet.
[04:36] Renee (Security): What about data residency? Our logs and prompts can't leave EU for some teams.
[04:44] Priya (SE): You can pin routes to region and use private control plane with VPC options. For Private we can deploy in your VPC and enforce egress rules.
[04:58] Alex (AE): One of our customers did a hybrid: hosted for low-volume teams, dedicated for high-throughput search. It reduced overall cost while meeting latency SLAs.
[05:12] Samir (CTO): Walk me through a failure mode — if the dedicated pool saturates, how fast is the fallback and what does that look like?
[05:24] Priya (SE): Fallbacks are policy driven. You can set immediate fallback to a cheaper model variant or route to another region. There's also a graceful degrade option that returns a cached response for a short time window. The routing is sub-second in our tests.
[05:42] Tom (SRE): Any risk of double-billing if requests are retried across pools?
[05:48] Jordan (Product): No, the platform marks attempts and billing attribution stays with the original project key; retries due to fallback are counted separately but annotated in the audit logs for reconciliation.
[06:02] [pause, typing]
[06:12] Priya (SE): I'm going to flip to the policy editor — it's JSON-backed but the Console gives templates. Here you can author a policy: match by project key, set min-reservation, burst-cap, fallback-model, and set metric alarms.
[06:30] Priya (SE): Example snippet — "project:search-service, reservation:60pct, burst:2x, fallback:search-small-quantized" — that's how we keep search fast while letting embeddings consume leftover capacity.
[06:46] Lena (Platform Eng): That fallback model — it's quantized, so lower quality? How do we monitor quality regressions?
[06:54] Jordan (Product): Redwood Optimize ties evals to rollout. You can attach a prompt set and monitor semantic similarity or hallucination rates. If quality drops, the policy can auto-revert or notify the owners.
[07:10] Renee (Security): For auditability, can we export raw token-level logs to our SIEM?
[07:18] Priya (SE): Yes, log streaming is configurable. For Private and Dedicated you can ship to your logging endpoint; hosted has a secure export option with retention tiers.
[07:30] Samir (CTO): Cost predictability — we need per-team invoices. Does Redwood expose per-project cost breakdowns?
[07:38] Maya (CSM): Yep, Console has per-key usage and token cost breakdowns. You can also set quotas that prevent over-run and alert when thresholds approach.
[07:50] Tom (SRE): Ok demo question — can you show a simulated spike?
[07:56] Priya (SE): Yes I'll trigger a synthetic load from the demo harness. watch the Dashboard on the right.
[08:10] [synthetic load starts - background beeps]
[08:22] Priya (SE): You can see embeddings-batch ramps up, we hit the embeddings slice burst window, then the fairburst allocator allows short runway, and once the org cap nears, search-service is preserved by reservation.
[08:44] Samir (CTO): Nice, what happened to the batch requests that exceeded the burst? queued or rejected?
[08:52] Priya (SE): The excess got backpressured — they see 429 with retry-after headers, or you can opt to queue for X seconds depending on SLA.
[09:04] Lena (Platform Eng): Those 429s — do they include a trace id for correlation?
[09:10] Priya (SE): Yes, every response contains request ids and route ids; you can correlate across logs.
[09:18] Tom (SRE): Can we enforce per-team concurrency limits across all regions? we have a microservice that fans out globally.
[09:26] Priya (SE): You can set global concurrency caps on project keys; routing policies will honor global caps and do region-aware balancing.
[09:36] Samir (CTO): If we want to run a pilot, what's the smallest commitment?
[09:42] Alex (AE): For pilots we usually do a 2-week pilot with a bench harness and a small dedicated pool if you want deterministic latency, or purely hosted with traffic shaping. We can size it around your expected qps.
[09:56] Renee (Security): For legal, we need a DPA and HIPAA addendum — do you support that?
[10:04] Alex (AE): We have templates; for enterprise/private deals we sign DPAs and addenda. I'll coordinate with legal.
[10:12] [brief cross talk about calendar slots]
[10:24] Priya (SE): back to Console — here's the alerting page. You can set alert on percent of org cap used, per-project error rates, and model quality regressions.
[10:36] Jordan (Product): Also, there is sticky routing — you can pin a session to a model variant for the duration of a user session to avoid cold-start variance.
[10:48] Samir (CTO): How do you charge when we use multi-region fallback? is there egress cost surcharge?
[10:56] Alex (AE): Usage is counted per token and region; cross-region egress would be charged as usual. We'll include a cost scenario in the pricing packet.
[11:08] Lena (Platform Eng): Do you have Terraform or IaC for key provisioning?
[11:14] Priya (SE): Yes we have Terraform provider and a REST API. Keys can be created programmatically and bound to policies.
[11:24] Tom (SRE): Any known gotchas when integrating with our CI/CD? we use ephemeral keys for test suites.
[11:32] Priya (SE): Ephemeral keys work — the Console can issue short-lived keys and you can also set revoke hooks.
[11:40] [slight laughter]
[11:44] Samir (CTO): Ok curious: do you have examples of namespace topologies that map to chargeback models?
[11:54] Maya (CSM): Yes — common patterns: per-product project keys (charge to product team), per-environment keys (charge to infra), and org-level metering for shared infra. We can share a template chargeback spreadsheet.
[12:10] Samir (CTO): Please do.
[12:14] Alex (AE): We'll attach that.
[12:18] Priya (SE): One more demo point — the rollout console for model swaps. You can do canary, A/B, or gradual ramp tied to policy. If a canary fails QA metrics, the platform auto-rolls back.
[12:34] Lena (Platform Eng): Can the rollback be triggered by either latency or semantic eval?
[12:40] Jordan (Product): Both. You can compose alarms from multiple signals.
[12:46] Renee (Security): Quick question on encryption at rest across components — is KV cache encrypted?
[12:54] Priya (SE): Yes, caches on Dedicated/Private are encrypted at rest and keys are controlled by KMS. On hosted the caches are managed, and we have encryption at rest with provider-managed keys unless you use Bring-Your-Own-Key.
[13:08] Tom (SRE): Are there rate limit algorithms exposed — token bucket, leaky bucket, or hybrid?
[13:16] Priya (SE): We support token-bucket for token quotas, leaky-bucket style smoothing for concurrency, and a hybrid fairshare allocator for org-level fairness.
[13:30] Samir (CTO): Anything special for embeddings billing? token vs vector units?
[13:36] Jordan (Product): Embeddings are billed per vector unit plus a compute factor for batch transforms; Console shows both components.
[13:46] [brief pause]
[13:56] Priya (SE): I'll demo the API side quickly — calling /v1/generate with project key header, response includes route id and model meta.
[14:08] Priya (SE): Example curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <project-key>" and the header x-redwood-route-id. If you hit limits, you'll get 429 and a retry-after template.
[14:22] Tom (SRE): For retries, is there an idempotency token pattern? We have lights-out workers that retry aggressively.
[14:30] Priya (SE): Use idempotency keys for mutating calls; for generation calls, retries are usually safe but annotated. You can also use the request id to dedupe at your side.
[14:44] Samir (CTO): Ok switching to procurement — timeline? We're aiming to decide by mid-September.
[14:52] Alex (AE): That fits. Pilot in early September, contract in late September.
[14:58] [background typing]
[15:10] Priya (SE): I'm pulling up the Optimizer suggestions — for your workload we recommend quantized variants for nightly embeddings, a small dedicated pool for search, and aggressive prefix caching on search queries to reduce token spend.
[15:28] Lena (Platform Eng): How much token savings with prefix caching? any ballpark?
[15:34] Jordan (Product): Depending on query re-use, 20-60% token reduction on search workloads. We'll give a tailored estimate.
[15:44] Samir (CTO): Security — can we restrict Console access per team? RBAC?
[15:50] Priya (SE): Yes, RBAC with SSO (SAML/OIDC), roles for reader/operator/admin, and you can limit per-project visibility.
[15:58] Renee (Security): Do you have attestations for pen-tests?
[16:04] Alex (AE): We have pen-test summaries and can share redacted reports under NDA.
[16:12] Tom (SRE): If we run a benchmark in our environment, how does telemetry get back to Redwood for support?
[16:20] Priya (SE): We can stream metrics or you can upload artifacts. For pilots we usually set a shared dashboard.
[16:30] Samir (CTO): Anything else we should be aware of for scaling to 10s of thousands of qps?
[16:38] Jordan (Product): Autoscaling, shard-aware routing, and pre-warmed caches. Also consider model parallelism and quantization to reduce load.
[16:48] [brief silence]
[16:54] Maya (CSM): quick recap: we'll send pricing, SOC2, pilot runbook and chargeback template.
[17:02] Alex (AE): Samir, do you want a dedicated pool sized for initial pilot or start hosted?
[17:08] Samir (CTO): Let's do a small dedicated pool for search and host the rest. We'll confirm size after we see pricing.
[17:18] Alex (AE): Perfect. I'll include a couple of sizing options.
[17:24] Priya (SE): One final note — when you do key topologies, keep a staging org separate to validate policies before they touch production keys.
[17:34] Lena (Platform Eng): Noted.
[17:36] [closing remarks]
[17:42] Alex (AE): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and proposed pilot dates.
[17:48] Samir (CTO): Thanks y'all, appreciated the demo.
[17:52] [meeting ends]

References shared: [Pricing scenario spreadsheet link], [SOC2 summary doc link], [Pilot runbook draft link], [Chargeback template spreadsheet link].
